title: Introduce Go credential-hub + stream decorators; ergonomic retries and v1.8.0 bump
author: Evan Matthews
description:
Summary: Adds a compact credential hub plus stream decorator helpers to the Go SDK to unify auth retry behavior, provide per-stream retry presets, and improve ergonomics for long-lived streaming consumers. This PR converges parity with the TypeScript and Python SDKs' recent credential middleware work while remaining idiomatic for Go.

Motivation and context: Several customers and internal SDK teams requested a clearer path for multi-credential flows, prefetching, and per-stream retry tuning. Existing code duplicated token lookup logic across connectors and made stream cancellation/heartbeat coordination awkward. This change centralizes credential lookup/rotation into a small credential hub abstraction and adds lightweight stream decorators that wire retry, heartbeat, and graceful shutdown correctly.

What this changes: - Introduces credentials/hub.go (CredentialHub interface + concrete LRU-backed hub)
- Adds stream/decorators.go with Decorator chain primitives: WithRetryPreset, WithHeartbeat, WithCancelOnError
- Exposes a new ClientOption: WithCredentialHub(...) for DI
- Adds a RetryPreset type and a small registry; default presets match py/ts semantics (fast-retry, balanced, conservative)
- Tests: unit tests for hub eviction, token refresh race, decorator interaction; integration smoke that validates streaming reconnects under simulated token rotation
- Docs: sdk/go/README.md updated with migration guide and examples
- Version bumped to v1.8.0 with changelog entry

Checklist: - [x] CredentialHub abstraction implemented and tested
- [x] Stream decorators implemented and documented
- [x] Cross-SDK parity verified against TS/Py reference PRs
- [x] Benchmarked: ~0.8% median latency regression on cold-start removed; 3-5% throughput gain for hot reuse in curl-style workloads
- [x] Added release notes and migration guide

Migration notes: Consumers that previously provided custom token lookups to individual stream constructors should switch to creating a shared CredentialHub and pass it via WithCredentialHub. Backwards compatibility: Client constructors still accept the previous TokenProvider func; if both are present, the CredentialHub takes priority and falls back to provider for legacy paths.

review_thread: Priya Nair: Nice consolidation. Can we avoid global state in the LRU cache? Suggest passing a context-based eviction hook.
Evan Matthews: Good call — switched the LRU to be attached to the hub instance and added an OnEvict callback that accepts context. Tests updated.
Miguel Santos: CI noticed a data race in TestStreamDecorator_Order when run with -race. Root cause was shared timer in tests; please isolate timers.
Evan Matthews: Fixed — tests now use fakeclock.New and are hermetic under -race.
Jordan Lee: Approve after nits: docs example shows WithCredentialHub before WithRetryPreset; prefer a paragraph explaining ordering semantics.
ci_checks: bench: microbench streaming reuse — completed (attached artifact)
release_notes: Go SDK v1.8.0: Introduces CredentialHub for centralized token rotation + stream decorators for per-stream retry/heartbeat behavior. API ergonomic improvements (WithCredentialHub, RetryPreset registry). Backwards compatible; see migration guide in sdk/go/README.md.
notes_for_qa: Important QA scenarios: 1) Validate long-lived streams survive token rotation with and without CredentialHub 2) Ensure existing TokenProvider behavior still works as fallback 3) Run race detector and long-lived simulation to surface timing issues
performance_summary: Microbench results in artifacts/bench/995550 show negligible median latency change (~+0.2% on single-request cold start) and improved throughput (3-5%) for hot-path reused credentials. Memory overhead for the hub cache is ~512 bytes per cached entry in benchmark config.
migration_examples: Example: hub := credentials.NewHub(credentials.WithCapacity(64), credentials.WithPrefetch(true)); client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithCredentialHub(hub)) — then use stream := client.Stream(ctx, opts...)
notes: This PR was coordinated with the TypeScript PR 507246 and Python PR 772980 to align retry presets and semantics. The registries contain the same nominal presets but remain pluggable per-language.
